about: [10] Guy is a close-up of a young man slumped on a couch with heavy, half-closed eyes, flushed cheeks and a slow, satisfied smile, a crinkled snack bag in the corner of the frame. Everything about the face reads as very, very high, and the captions narrate the logic of someone in that state: solving problems that do not exist, getting confused by ordinary objects, or reaching profound conclusions about cereal. The name treats his state as a score, as in a ten out of ten. The joke is always the gap between how deep the thought feels to him and how pointless it looks to everyone else.
origin: The photo spread on Reddit as one of the advice animal image macros of the early 2010s, where it picked up nicknames like Really High Guy and Stoner Stanley.
usage:
Use the classic advice animal layout. The top box sets up an everyday situation in the third person (“goes to the kitchen for a snack”), and the bottom box delivers the spaced-out conclusion or misfire (“forgets why, makes a sandwich anyway”).

The best captions follow a broken but internally consistent train of thought, like turning down the radio to see better. Keep it about harmless confusion, forgetfulness and snack logic. Short lines suit his sleepy face; a long sentence ruins the pacing.
ideas: can't read the words on the menu
forgets what he wanted, closes it, opens it again
